verdict.rationale: The department's own docs say a tax professional can, with the client's authorization, review the client's filing and payment history, view bills and notices, and respond on their behalf. Businesses can also add employees as account users with different levels of access. This is a thin, glancing description of delegated scope, not a published rulebook of what third parties may and may not do. Missing for 10: named authorization forms (e.g., power-of-attorney forms), a defined catalogue of roles and access levels, an explicit list of actions third parties may not take, which signatures or attestations must stay personal, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: With your client’s authorization, you can review their filing and payment history, view copies of their bills and notices, and respond on their behalf.
add your employees as account users with different levels of access.
